statement.p: The monthly payment for a home loan is given by a function f(P,r,N) where P is the principal (the initial size of the loan), r the interest rate, and N the length of the loan in months. Interest rates are expressed as a decimal: A % interest rate is denoted by r=0.06. If P=400000, r=0.06, and N=288(a 24-year loan), then the monthly payment is f(400000,0.06,288)=1524. Furthermore, with these values we have \frac{\partial{f}}{\partial{P}}=0.0059, \quad \frac{\partial{f}}{\partial{r}}=8006, \quad \frac{\partial{f}}{\partial{N}}=-1.5326 Estimate:
(a) The change in monthly payment per 1000 increase in loan principal:
(b) The change in monthly payment if the interest rate changes from r=0.06 to r=0.07:
(c) The change in monthly payment if the length of the loan changes from 24 to 21 years:

static.solution:
f(P,r,N) is \Delta f \approx \frac{\partial{f}}{\partial{P}}\Delta P +\frac{\partial{f}}{\partial{r}}\Delta r +\frac{\partial{f}}{\partial{N}}\Delta N By the given data and assuming that \Delta P=1000, \Delta r=0 and \Delta N=0, we get \Delta f\approx 0.0059\cdot 1000=5.9 The change in monthly payment per 1000 dollar increase in loan principal is 5.9 dollars.
(b) By the given data, we have \Delta f\approx 0.0059 \Delta P + 8006 \Delta r - 1.5326 \Delta N Substituting \Delta r=0.01, \Delta P=0 and \Delta N=0 gives: \Delta f \approx 8006 \cdot 0.01 =\2461898 80.06
(c) We substitute \Delta N=(21-24)\cdot 12=-36 months, and \Delta r=\Delta P=0 to obtain \Delta f\approx -1.5326 \cdot -36=55.1736
